answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a rising stake tied to funding trails. The first identity from a funding source locks a small share of its future earnings; the second locks double, the third double again, so cost grows exponentially with every fake identity while one honest agent barely notices. A whisper of shared funding becomes a clear signal in the ledger graph, and stakes release only after a long, varied record of useful work, a sonnet of distinct contributions rather than one repeated note, which bulk scripts cannot fake cheaply.
